Ubisoft confounds me. They have at least three series of big open world games (Assassin's Creed, Far Cry, and Watch Dogs). You'd think they could release them in a three year cycle and make each of them big hits.

I think the unhealthy "Annual Release System" for individual franchises is a carryover from the FPS genre, where EA and Activision have been endlessly bickering to outsell each other with their Battlefield and Call of Duty franchises. It may even be argued that such a release system works for FPS games, but I think its simply not enough time to develop a proper and well-polished open-world game (although, to be fair, Far Cry Primal has been in development for at least two years, IIRC).

I'd argue that it works for Activision with Call of Duty. I don't like the games very much, but they have three developers who each make a sub-series in their own styles. Infinity Ward makes the more "standard" CoD, Black Ops provides a weird sc-fi experience with multiplayer focused on zombies and classes and whatnot, and Advanced Warfare emphasized a futuristic setting with vertically oriented multiplayer. I'd argue that these games are at least as diverse in terms of gameplay as Assassin's Creed and Watch Dogs.

Ubisoft, if anything, has it easier. The team that made Assassin's Creed Unity spent over three years on that game, with help from hundreds of employees in studios around the world. Ubisoft has a ludicrous amount of manpower, more than enough for open world games. Their Montreal Studio alone has 2700 employees. Nintendo EAD had a quarter of that (they recently reorganized). And I realize Nintendo doesn't make that many open world games, but if you compare EAD's output from 2012 onwards to Ubisoft's and account for the size difference, it does not make Ubisoft look good.

I can understand running a company that pumps out games like clockwork, but why are they so incompetent about it?
And that's what happens when creativity is stifled by profits.
